counterfactual.change: changed single field bodies[0].e from 0.912790531673785 to 0.0; with inelastic collision the same geometry/speed/dt no longer creates energy (energy stays ~57 J) so hypothesis that restitution handling creates energy is confirmed

explanation: Energy gain at high-speed wall collision with high restitution. Body 0 approaches thin vertical wall (x=10.6, w=0.1) at ~38.89 m/s (step 6, vx +38.887). After collision at step 7 vx is reversed to -41.33 and speed increases to 41.34, so kinetic energy exceeds incoming energy despite e=0.912<1 and no controller work. Allowed = 900.41 (E0 814.01) but recorded 911.94. Counterfactual with same scenario but e=0 shows inelastic collision correctly dissipates energy and passes, proving violation is caused by restitution/collision impulse logic adding energy (e.g., incorrect impulse magnitude, double correction, or substep integration error on fast body hitting thin wall).
vision_note: The blue circle travels rapidly from the left toward the thin vertical wall, reaching contact at the wall's upper edge by step 6. At step 7 it remains at/overlapping the wall rather than cleanly rebounding leftward, showing a collision that fails to dissipate energy and instead produces the impulsive reversal described.
